chapter: Bird's world, singers and the new music
title: The Brew Moore Blue Note date and playing better now
summary: He says he plays better now but the body may not follow.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: And then I'm always coming back to that date which I think is one of the great unsung dates, with Brew Moore and J.J. Johnson, because there you're playing very harmonically, intricate, very beautiful things...
Yeah. Well, I've got that album here, where I was playing with... The Savoy thing you're taking about, right?
No, now I'm talking about that Blue Note date that we talked about before...
Yeah, I have that here, up with the McGhee records... It was all right, I guess. I don't know... I think I'm playing better now than I ever played, but I can't be my own critic.
Well, you gain knowledge over the years...
Or it comes out in your playing, all the things that
you've accumulated in your mind and in your living experience, and that affects the way you play.
Yeah. And also, in the meantime, your body might not be able to do what you know you can do. And if it ain't in good shape, it ain't gonna make it.
